chunks: He passes the pathway of this world in a praiseworthy manner,
and he advances the provisions of the Hereafter in a happy manner,
and he hastens out of fear,
and he moves briskly during leisure (short time),
and he monitors his tomorrow during his today,
and he looks forward ahead of him.

So Paradise is sufficient as a reward and attainment, and Hell is sufficient as a punishment and consequence! And Allah is sufficient as an Avenger and Helper! And the Book is sufficient as an advocate and opponent.

key_terms.زَادَ: Provisions (for the journey to the Hereafter)

ai.seo_question: How does Ali (peace be upon him) describe the ideal attitude towards this world and the Hereafter?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Al-Gharra*, Imam Ali employs rhythmic parallelism to urge believers to traverse the transient world with honor and secure their eternal abode through proactive piety. The text underscores the sufficiency of Paradise and Hell as ultimate outcomes, while affirming Allah’s justice and the Qur'an’s role as a witness, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *Zuhd* (asceticism) and *Muraqaba* (mindfulness of God). This exhortation serves as a foundational ethical guideline for balancing worldly duties with spiritual preparation for the Hereafter.
